observation.visible_scene: A wide desert landscape under a massive, dark storm cloud that fills most of the sky. A broad gray rain/outflow column descends from the cloud base in the left-center of the frame, reaching the ground. On the right horizon a low mountain range is partly veiled by a tan dust band. The foreground is flat scrubland with scattered bushes, and the camera viewpoint and ground line stay fixed throughout.
visible_changes: The dust plume on the right grows markedly taller and denser over the excerpt, starting as a thin low haze at the mountain base (t=0) and becoming a thick, rolling brown wall that rises well above the ridgeline by the end (t=2.67).
The dust front advances leftward along the ground, spreading from the right edge toward the center foreground and increasingly obscuring the mountains.
The base of the central rain column thickens and blends with the rising dust near the horizon as the segment progresses.
Cloud texture and shading shift subtly overhead, with the dark shelf/anvil on the right appearing to creep slightly leftward, while the overall cloud mass persists.
A bright sunlit patch at the lower part of the rain column remains visible throughout.
The foreground terrain and shrubs do not change position, indicating no camera pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The initial trigger or earlier development of the dust front before t=0.
Whether the dust wall eventually overtakes the rain column or the camera position.
The full duration and intensity evolution of the rainfall beyond the cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the slow cloud-base motion on the right is true translation or internal cloud evolution (deformation/occlusion).
Exact physical identity of the descending column (rain vs. virga) and of the right-side plume (haboob/outflow boundary) cannot be confirmed from imagery alone.
Minor frame-to-frame differences in cloud shape may be lighting/contrast changes rather than movement.
